A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GiFT and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original code-generation experiments with DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B and CodeLlama-7B, including Pass@1 results, code-diversity measurements, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds experiments testing Gibbs-derived descriptions and perplexity-guided selection in baseline methods.

M1.justification: Sections 3-4 and Algorithm 1 retain GiFT's alternating code-description generation, correctness filtering, perplexity-weighted selection, and fine-tuning procedure. The rewritten exponential formula is equivalent notation; dynamic sampling is proposed only as future work.

E1.justification: Both versions use APPS+ Introductory and Interview, MBPP-sanitized training with MBPP+ testing, and CodeInsight, all in Python. The added controls reuse this coverage; OSS-Instruct is explicitly mentioned as unevaluated.

E2.justification: The main RFT and RFT+RD comparisons remain. v2 adds RFT+GiFT Desc., using descriptions from one Gibbs step, in Figure 4 and RFT with perplexity-guided selection in Figure 9. These are targeted extensions within the existing comparator families.

E3.justification: v2 adds a single-step description-generation control and selection-on/off comparisons for RFT and GiFT, reported over iterations 1-2 with DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B. Existing splits, Pass@1 evaluation, three-iteration main experiments, generation budgets, and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figures 4 and 9 test whether Gibbs-derived descriptions close the RFT+RD gap and whether perplexity-guided selection also benefits RFT. These extend the existing analyses. The K-sensitivity study already appeared in v1 Appendix D.3 and is merely moved into Section 5.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2 retains three random seeds, 1234, 12345, and 123456, and the existing plots retain standard-deviation bands. No additional uncertainty-estimation procedure, significance test, or changed run count is reported.

E6.justification: Table 1 and all original plotted results are retained. New Figure 4 shows Gibbs-derived descriptions improving RFT+RD, with GiFT ahead at iteration 2; Figure 9 adds selection-ablation outcomes. Figure 9's APPS panel labels appear reversed relative to the corresponding Figure 3 curves, limiting dataset-specific interpretation of those new results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and expectation/variance derivations remain unchanged. The added remark about input sensitivity interprets the existing variance term without introducing a formal assumption or derivation; replacing exponential notation with exp is mathematically equivalent.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: marginal-distribution sampling through GiFT, perplexity-guided selection, and empirical superiority across two LLMs and four benchmarks. The introduction adds a numerical performance summary without changing these claims' scope.

C2.justification: A new Limitations section explicitly addresses approximately 7B/Python-only evaluation, dependence on supplied test cases, and additional summarization cost, with possible future remedies. v2 also adds explanations linking input sensitivity to diversity and multiple code origins to GiFT's advantage over the single-step control.

D1.justification: The abstract newly reports source-code availability and provides a repository link. Figure 2 identifies its example as MBPP-sanitized/6. Existing prompt templates, checkpoint links, hyperparameters, optimizer settings, and hardware details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds CodeT, B4, and DSTC citations when discussing generated tests as a possible remedy for test-case dependence. Section 2's related-work taxonomy and GiFT's principal research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds localized explanatory passages, Limitations and Acknowledgement sections, and expanded author-contact information, and moves the K-sensitivity discussion into the main text. Most existing prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 4 and 9, moves the existing K-sensitivity figure into Section 5, and relocates or renumbers other figures, prompt tables, dataset statistics, and Algorithm 1. Original graphics are retained. The new Figure 9 has an apparent APPS panel-label inconsistency.

improvement.justification: The new controls address questions left open in v1 about description quality and the contribution of data selection. Together with explicit limitations and code-access information, they improve empirical scrutiny and transparency. The gain is limited by the apparent APPS label reversal in Figure 9, which weakens the clarity of that added analysis.
